literal: Xiaoyou at the capital accumulated years, with law self-guarding, very marked in reputation.
idiomatic: Xiaoyou served many years as capital intendant, kept the law himself, and won a strong reputation.

literal: Yet his nature lacked backbone, good at serving power and influence — upright ones ridiculed him for it.
idiomatic: Yet he lacked backbone and courted the powerful; the upright mocked him for it.

literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao, according to precedent rank was lowered, enfeoffed Marquis of Linhuai county, appointed Honored Grandee of Light.
idiomatic: At the start of Qi Tianbao his rank was reduced by precedent to Marquis of Linhuai county and Honored Grandee of Light.

literal: Second year winter, ordered into Jinyang Palace, went out and with Yuan Huiye was together harmed.
idiomatic: In the second winter he was summoned to Jinyang Palace and killed together with Yuan Huiye.

literal: Younger brother of the clan Fu, courtesy name Xiuhe, in youth had fine reputation.
idiomatic: His clansman younger brother Fu, courtesy Xiuhe, was famed in youth.

literal: Attendant-in-ordinary You Zhao, Governor of Bingzhou Gao Cong, Minister Cui Guang and others seeing Fu all said: "This child should match the great men of the age — pity our company is aged and declining, not reaching to see."
idiomatic: You Zhao, Gao Cong of Bingzhou, Cui Guang, and others said of him: "This boy will match the great men of the age — pity we are old and will not see it."

literal: Promoted in stages to concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He rose to concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

literal: Empress Dowager Ling at court, eunuchs interfering in government — Fu thereupon summarized through the ages famous consorts and worthy queens, altogether four scrolls, submitted them.
idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling ruled and eunuchs meddled, Fu compiled four scrolls of famous consorts and worthy empresses and presented them.

literal: Promoted to Left Vice Director.
idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director.

literal: Rouran lord Anagui having regained his state, his people greatly starved, together entering the passes — Anagui submitted a memorial requesting court relief.
idiomatic: When the Rouran lord Anagui recovered his realm his people starved and poured through the passes; Anagui asked the court for relief.

literal: Edict made Fu Northern Route Commissioner, going there to relieve and comfort; Fu submitted a convenient-terms memorial saying:
idiomatic: The court made Fu Northern Route Commissioner to bring aid; he memorialized:

literal: Leather-clothed people have never grain-eaten — should follow custom and take advantage, saving what they lack.
idiomatic: "Leather-clad peoples have never lived on grain; aid should follow their ways and supply what they lack.

literal: Formerly in Han Jianwu, the Shanyu submitted to the passes — at the time transferred Hedong rice twenty-five thousand hu, cattle and sheep thirty-six thousand head to give them.
idiomatic: In Han Jianwu, when the Shanyu came to the frontier, the court sent twenty-five thousand hu of Hedong grain and thirty-six thousand head of cattle and sheep.

literal: This then is former age harmonizing with the Rong, comforting the new and softening the distant — the long strategy.
idiomatic: That was the old policy of pacifying the Rong and winning the newly submitted.

literal: Beg to use breeding cows producing sheep, paste their mouth food.
idiomatic: Grant breeding cattle and ewes and feed them dairy.

literal: Moreover animal husbandry multiplying is what they are skilled at;
idiomatic: Herding is their strength;

literal: fur and blood's profit, favor joining clothes and food.
idiomatic: wool and meat serve both clothing and food.

literal: Also the Secretariat memorial said: if they still dwell in the seven provinces, broadly place them as width allows.
idiomatic: The Secretariat also proposed settling them across seven provinces wherever space allowed.

literal: Your subject considers human feeling clings to roots — would they willingly move inward?
idiomatic: I say people cling to home — will they willingly move inland?

literal: If following your subject's request, giving relief mixed livestock, loving roots and honoring native place, they will surely return to old lands.
idiomatic: If you follow my plan and give mixed herds, cherishing home, they will return to their old lands.

literal: If not so, forbidding and detaining increases harm.
idiomatic: Otherwise detention only deepens the harm.

literal: Suppose forced migration — the affair is not a long-term plan.
idiomatic: Forced migration is no long-term policy.

literal: Why?
idiomatic: Why?

literal: Human face, beast heart — going and staying hard to measure.
idiomatic: Human faces hide beast hearts; loyalty is hard to read.

literal: Having changed water and grass, illness and harm will be many;
idiomatic: Change their pasture and sickness multiplies;

literal: worry and distress leading to exhaustion, death will be very severe.
idiomatic: grief and want will kill many.

literal: Moreover the rest of their kind still are in sand and gravel;
idiomatic: Their kin remain in the desert;

literal: if they escape wild rage and turn back to old nests, they will surely ravage districts and towns, leaving poison to the common people.
idiomatic: if they break free and return, they will ravage the border and poison the people.

literal: Chaos and then blocking the passes — not as good as stopping it before it sprouts.
idiomatic: To seal the passes after chaos is worse than stopping the sprout.

literal: Also trade and transport rose in high antiquity, exchange proceeded in middle ages.
idiomatic: Trade is ancient; barter flourished in middle antiquity.

literal: Han with Hu connected, also established pass markets.
idiomatic: Han dealt with the Hu and set border markets.

literal: Now northerners obstructed by famine, life suspended over ditch and ravine;
idiomatic: Now the north starves; lives hang over the abyss.

literal: beyond public giving, they must seek market exchange.
idiomatic: Beyond public relief they must trade.

literal: If they wish to request, it is fitting to be heard and permitted.
idiomatic: If they ask to buy, grant it.

literal: Also said:
idiomatic: He also wrote:

literal: Managing great affairs does not calculate small names, plotting distant does not bind near profit.
idiomatic: "Great undertakings ignore petty reputation; distant plans do not cling to immediate gain.

literal: Though Rong and Di decline and flourish differ by generation, the feeling of rebellion and submission can roughly be discussed and examined.
idiomatic: Barbarian strength shifts with each age, but their pattern of submission and revolt can be weighed.

literal: Zhou's northern campaign barely obtained middle regulation;
idiomatic: Zhou's northern campaigns barely achieved middling success;

literal: Han House's outer expansion only barely took the lower strategy.
idiomatic: Han outward expansion often took the lesser plan.

literal: Formerly at Dai capital, constantly was heavy defense — generals and commanders labor stopped, armored soldiers strength exhausted.
idiomatic: At the old capital Dai the frontier was always heavily garrisoned; generals wore out and soldiers drained away.

literal: Considering former generations suffered it, strength could not reach.
idiomatic: Past dynasties suffered this because force alone could not finish the work.

literal: Today heaven's mandate is great Wei, chaos and ruin are over there.
idiomatic: Now heaven favors great Wei; their disorder is their own.

literal: Court droops heaven-covering favor, broadly great-making virtue, gathering their scattered and lost, rite sending ordering return — should at this time well think distant strategy.
idiomatic: The court spreads sheltering grace and vast mercy, gathers their scattered, and sends them home with ritual — this is the moment for far-sighted policy.

literal: Your subject considers principle though ten thousand changes, can be viewed in one observation;
idiomatic: Principle shifts in ten thousand ways yet may be read in one glance;

literal: coming affairs though suspended, easy to use past to divine.
idiomatic: the future, though uncertain, may be divined from the past.

literal: Formerly in Han Xuan's age, Huhanye submitted to the passes — Han sent Dong Zhong and Han Chang leading border commandery soldiers and horses, escorting out beyond Shuofang, thereupon remaining to guard and assist.
idiomatic: In Han Xuandi's time Huhanye came to the passes; Han sent Dong Zhong and Han Chang with border troops to escort him beyond Shuofang and left guards to assist.

literal: Also in Guangwu's time, again ordered Central Gentlemen Duan Bin to set Pacification clerks, following the Shanyu's place, examining movement and stillness.
idiomatic: Under Guangwu, Central Gentlemen Duan Bin placed Pacification clerks with the Shanyu to watch his movements.

literal: These all are guarding the auspicious's primary tortoise, settling the border's winning strategy.
idiomatic: Those were the tortoise of good fortune and the winning border strategy.

literal: Considering today's court's achievement, not reduced from former times; Rouran state's exhaustion, also the same as yesterday.
idiomatic: Today's court is no weaker than those ages; Rouran's exhaustion matches yesterday's.

literal: Should follow former completed plans, roughly follow old affairs, borrowing their idle lands, hearing them field and pasture.
idiomatic: Follow the old completed plans: lend idle land and let them herd.

literal: Roughly set official subordinates, displaying mutual comfort and soothing.
idiomatic: Place officials to show care.

literal: Strictly warn border soldiers, to display protection and guard.
idiomatic: Warn the border troops to protect them visibly.

literal: Driving with benevolence and breadth, tethering with long policy.
idiomatic: Rule them with kindness and bind them with long policy.

literal: Making close not reach deceit, distant not tolerate rebellion.
idiomatic: Keep the near from deceit and the far from revolt.

literal: Now Northern Garrison generals, old constant saying one man replaces outer rotation, thereupon ordered defense and inspection.
idiomatic: Northern Garrison generals still rotate one officer to the frontier for inspection.

literal: This is called the Son of Heaven has the Way, defense kept in the four barbarians.
idiomatic: That is what it means to say: when the Son of Heaven holds the Way, defense lies in the four barbarians.

literal: Also said:
idiomatic: He also wrote:

literal: Forefathers had heart of seizing others' — treating submission like receiving a strong enemy.
idiomatic: "Forefathers kept the heart of conquest even toward those who submitted.

literal: Martial not only seeking outer, also to guard inner.
idiomatic: Arms serve not only the frontier but the interior.

literal: If following placement division and assignment to the various provinces and garrisons, distant and far, not transport and delivery can reach — repentant rebellion's feeling, change arising hard to measure.
idiomatic: If we split and assign them among distant provinces, supply cannot follow and repentant revolt may arise unmeasured.

literal: Also dwelling people raising livestock, cloth spread on original wilds — Rong and Yi nature greedy, seeing then thinking theft;
idiomatic: Their herds lie open on the steppe; barbarians are greedy and theft tempts them;

literal: guarding them strict here, few soldiers cannot bear.
idiomatic: guarding one place leaves too few men elsewhere.

literal: At confused currents' juncture, easy mutually to violate.
idiomatic: In turbulent times clashes come easily.

literal: Driving them back to roots, not necessarily pleased to go; assigning within provinces inner move, again not willing to follow.
idiomatic: Drive them home and they may not wish to go; move them inland and they will refuse.

literal: Since it is thus, expense must be great.
idiomatic: Either way the cost will be vast.

literal: Court did not permit.
idiomatic: The court did not accept.

literal: Fu held white martial banner consoling Anagui between Rouxuan and Huaihuang two garrisons.
idiomatic: Fu carried the white peace banner to console Anagui between Rouxuan and Huaihuang.

literal: Anagui's host numbered three hundred thousand, secretly had different intent, thereupon detained Fu.
idiomatic: Anagui's following was said to number three hundred thousand; he secretly harbored other plans and detained Fu.

literal: Loaded in covered cart, daily given one sheng of curdled milk, one section of meat.
idiomatic: They loaded him in a covered cart and gave him daily a sheng of curd and a portion of meat.

literal: Each gathering his host, seating Fu in the carriage compartment, calling him Route Commissioner, greatly adding ritual respect.
idiomatic: Whenever he assembled his men he seated Fu in the carriage compartment, called him Route Commissioner, and treated him with great honor.

literal: Anagui thereupon passed south, reaching old capital.
idiomatic: Anagui then marched south to the old capital.

literal: Later sent Fu and others back, thereupon submitted memorial apologizing.
idiomatic: Later he sent Fu and the others back and submitted an apology.

literal: Relevant offices because of Fu's affair handed down to Court of Justice, Vice Director Gao Qianzhi saying Fu disgraced the mandate, sentenced Fu to exile crime.
idiomatic: The ministries referred Fu to the Court of Justice; Vice Director Gao Qianzhi said Fu had disgraced his commission and urged exile.

literal: Later appointed Governor of Jizhou.
idiomatic: He was later made Governor of Jizhou.

literal: Fu urged mulberry and farming lessons, within the borders called kind father, neighboring provinces titled divine lord.
idiomatic: Fu promoted sericulture and farming; his province called him kind father, neighboring ones divine lord.

literal: Earlier, provincials Zhang Mengdu, Zhang Hongjian, Ma Pan, Cui Dulian, Zhang Shuxu, Cui Chou, Zhang Tianyi, Cui Sizhe and eight others — all garrisoned fortresses in forest wilds, not serving the king's command, provinces and commanderies called them Eight Kings.
idiomatic: Eight men of the province — Zhang Mengdu, Zhang Hongjian, Ma Pan, Cui Dulian, Zhang Shuxu, Cui Chou, Zhang Tianyi, and Cui Sizhe — had held wild fortresses and defied the throne; the region called them the Eight Kings.

literal: When Fu arrived, all requested entering the cities, willing to die to offer strength.
idiomatic: When Fu arrived they all entered the cities and offered their lives in service.

literal: Later was trapped by Ge Rong, seized by Rong.
idiomatic: Later Ge Rong captured him.

literal: Elder brother You was Defense City Metropolitan Commander, elder brother's son Li was Recording Office Attendant.
idiomatic: His brother You was Defense City Metropolitan Commander; his nephew Li was Recording Office Attendant.

literal: Rong wished first to harm son Li — Fu requested first death to redeem son Li, knocking head blood flowing, Rong thereupon spared him.
idiomatic: Rong meant to kill Li first; Fu begged to die in his stead, knocking his head until blood ran, and Rong spared Li.

literal: Again greatly gathering generals and soldiers, deliberating his death affair.
idiomatic: Rong again gathered his officers to decide Fu's fate.

literal: Fu's brothers each falsely accused themselves drawing fault, competing to be the one to die.
idiomatic: Fu's brothers each claimed the fault as his own and vied to die.

literal: Also Mengdu, Pan Shao and several hundred men all knocked heads approaching execution, requesting to spare the lord.
idiomatic: Mengdu, Pan Shao, and hundreds more bowed their heads for execution, begging Rong to spare their lord.

literal: Rong said: "These are Wei's sincere subjects and righteous knights."
idiomatic: Rong said, "These are Wei's loyal and righteous men."

literal: Altogether those together imprisoned five hundred men, all obtained exemption.
idiomatic: Five hundred held with him were all released.

literal: When Rong died, returned and removed to Governor of Jizhou.
idiomatic: After Rong's death he returned as Governor of Jizhou.

literal: Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, invested Fu Eastern Route Commissioner, Prince of Pengcheng.
idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang he made Fu Eastern Route Commissioner and Prince of Pengcheng.

literal: Fu sealed Hao's rebellious letter and sent to court — the Son of Heaven praised it.
idiomatic: Fu sealed Hao's rebel letters and sent them to court; the emperor praised him.

literal: When Hao died, enfeoffed Fu Marquis of Wannian township.
idiomatic: When Hao died, Fu was enfeoffed Marquis of Wannian township.

literal: At the end of Yong'an, musical instruments incomplete — Emperor Zhuangang ordered Fu to supervise ritual regulations.
idiomatic: At the end of Yong'an the ritual instruments were broken; Emperor Zhuangang ordered Fu to supervise the regulations.

literal: Fu submitted a memorial saying:
idiomatic: Fu memorialized:

literal: Formerly in great harmony, Secretariat Supervisor Gao Lu, Grand Music Master Gongsun Chong repaired and made metal and stone — several decades between, then memorialized completion.
idiomatic: "In the great Taihe era, Secretariat Supervisor Gao Lu and Grand Music Master Gongsun Chong rebuilt the bells and stones; decades passed before they reported success.

literal: At the time greatly gathered Confucian scholars, examining their gain and loss.
idiomatic: Confucian scholars were gathered to judge the result.

literal: Grand Minister of Ritual Liu Fang requested separate construction — long afterward then completed.
idiomatic: Grand Minister Liu Fang asked for a separate set; long after, that too was finished.

literal: Again summoned dukes and ministers to measure and collate whether fitting, debaters boiling, none having what to follow.
idiomatic: Dukes and ministers were summoned to compare them; debate boiled and no consensus held.

literal: Deng received imperial edict and command, all seen applied.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen ordered both adopted.

literal: Past year great army entered Luoyang, war horses crossing — all musical instruments, lost almost completely.
idiomatic: Last year the great army entered Luoyang; in the fighting nearly all instruments were lost.

literal: Your subject reaching Grand Music Office, asked Grand Music Master Zhang Qian'gui and others, saying from former coming down, set palace suspension four cases, wooden tiger six frames, northeast frame compiled Yellow Bell's chime fourteen.
idiomatic: At the Grand Music Office, Grand Music Master Zhang Qian'gui told me that since former times the court kept four cases of palace bells, six wooden frames, and on the northeast frame fourteen Yellow Bell chimes.

literal: Though the instrument's name Yellow Bell, the sound in fact Yize;
idiomatic: Though named Yellow Bell, they actually sound Yize;

literal: Examining sound regulation, not very harmonious in rhyme.
idiomatic: and measured against the pitch standard they are badly out of tune.
